Weights of Markov Traces on Hecke Algebras∗
R.C. Orellana
November 16, 2021
Abstract
We compute the weights, i.e. the values at the minimal idempotents, for the Markov
trace on the Hecke algebra of type Bn and type Dn. In order to prove the weight
formula, we deﬁne representations of the Hecke algebra of type B onto a reduced
Hecke Algebra of type A. To compute the weights for type D we use the inclusion of
the Hecke algebra of type D into the Hecke algebra of type B.

blocks.content: Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $0$. The algebra of $n\times n$ matrices over $F$ is denoted by $M_n(F)=M_n$. Let $A\subset B$ be an inclusion of semisimple algebras. Then $A=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m A_i$ and $B=\bigoplus_{j=1}^lB_j$, with $A_i\cong M_{a_i}$, $B_j\cong M_{b_j}$ and $a_i,\ b_j\in \mathbb{N}$. blocks.title: Partitions and Standard Tableaux
blocks.content: A *partition* of $n$ is a sequence of positive numbers $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots, \alpha_k)$ such that $\alpha_1\geq \alpha_2\geq \ldots \geq \alpha_k \geq 0$ and $n=|\alpha|=\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\ldots +\alpha_k$. The $\alpha_i$'s are called the *parts* of $\alpha$, and the number of nonzero parts of $\alpha$ is called the *length* of $\alpha$, denoted by $l(\alpha)$. If we say $l(\alpha)\leq r_1$, then we we will mean that there are $s\leq r_1$ nonzero parts and the remaining $r_1-s$ are equal to zero. blocks.title: Markov Traces on the Hecke Algebra of type $B$
blocks.content: In this section we give the necessary background on Markov traces. We refer the reader to [@gl] or [@g] for the details. A *trace* function on $H_{\infty}(q,Q)$ is a $\mathbb{C}(q,Q)$-linear map $\phi:H_{\infty}(q,Q)\longrightarrow \mathbb{C}(q,Q)$ such that $\phi (hh')=\phi (h'h)$ for all $h,h' \in H_{\infty}(q,Q)$. This definition is in fact valid for any associative algebra over a commutative ground ring.
